title: Personalized Federated Learning using Hypernetworks
layout_note: Left panel: a grey server box in the centre with three client boxes to its left, below and right, each linked by a pair of opposite arrows. Right panel: the same exchange for one client i, with that client's inputs entering from above and its loss leaving below.
grouping: No containers; panels are separated by whitespace. Each client has its own fill colour (pink, peach, lilac) and the math labels on its two arrows are set in that same colour; the server is neutral grey.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with dark outlines, each holding only a function in math notation (h(.; phi) for the server, f_k(.; theta_k) for clients). Each link is a pair of thin parallel black arrows: the one toward the client labelled theta_k, the one back labelled Delta theta_k. Math-only labels, no words.
proposed_highlight: Nothing is marked as new; the whole figure is the protocol: the server box produces each client's weights, so what is sent down (theta_k) and up (Delta theta_k) is the content, coloured per client.
lesson: Draw each client link as a pair of opposite arrows labelled with what travels - weights down, weight update up - and set those labels in the client's own fill colour so the exchange is legible per client without a legend.
notes: Year = arXiv preprint year. Remembered as ICML 2021, not confirmed by the v1 PDF or the arXiv metadata read here.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture other = a server-side hypernetwork h(.; phi) that generates each client's weights

insights.structure: Two unframed panels separated by whitespace: left, a grey server box in the centre with three client boxes to its left, below and right; right, the exchange for one client i, server on the left and client on the right.
insights.data: Boxes hold only functions in math notation (h(.; phi), f_k(.; theta_k)); each link is a pair of thin opposite arrows labelled theta_k (to the client) and Delta theta_k (back); in the right panel inputs v_i and x enter from above and the loss L_i leaves below the client.
insights.emphasis: Each client has its own fill (pink, peach, lilac) and the math labels on its arrows are set in the same colour, so what travels per client is legible without a legend; the server stays neutral grey.
insights.flow: Hub-and-spoke on the left with bidirectional arrow pairs; the right panel reads top to bottom (inputs down into h and f_i, loss out below) with the theta_i / Delta theta_i exchange horizontal.
insights.avoid: Math-only labels with no words: a reader who has not read the text cannot tell that h is a hypernetwork or that v_i is a client embedding.

arrangement.units: two unframed panels (overview of all clients, detail of one client) separated by whitespace; boxes are flat rounded rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols v_i and x with arrows down (right panel)
arrangement.losses_at: below the client box in the right panel (L_i)
arrangement.shared: the grey server box h(.; phi) appears in both panels
